suggestions.rationale: Sleep disruption is a core PTSD symptom, and claims frequently explore whether a sleep-disordered breathing diagnosis is proximately due to or aggravated by the service-connected psychiatric condition.
evidenceGaps: Sleep study (polysomnography) confirming a current sleep apnea diagnosis
Medical opinion linking the sleep condition to PTSD rather than to independent risk factors
Treatment records documenting sleep complaints alongside PTSD symptoms

suggestions.rationale: Depressive symptoms often co-occur with PTSD. Note that VA generally evaluates all service-connected mental health conditions under a single rating, so this may affect the existing evaluation rather than add a separate one.
evidenceGaps: Mental health records distinguishing depressive symptoms from existing PTSD symptoms
Clarification of whether a separate diagnosis has been made by a qualified provider

sourceReferences.note: Avoidance of pyramiding; relevant when symptoms overlap.

suggestions.rationale: Headache complaints appear in some records where chronic stress and sleep deficit are documented. The connection is less direct than sleep or mood claims and generally needs a supporting medical opinion.
evidenceGaps: Neurology records or headache diagnosis from a qualified provider
Documentation of headache frequency, duration, and whether attacks are prostrating
Nexus opinion addressing causation or aggravation

suggestions.rationale: Sometimes explored where reflux symptoms are documented alongside psychiatric medication use. Medication-induced aggravation is a distinct theory from direct causation and should be stated explicitly.
evidenceGaps: Confirmed GERD diagnosis with documented symptoms
Complete medication history showing prescriptions for the service-connected condition
Opinion addressing whether medication side effects caused or aggravated the condition
